JPMorgan has put generative AI on the desks of 200,000-plus employees; at Citi, nearly 9 in 10 staff use AI tools. Wall Street stopped reading raw data by hand — most of us are still scrolling headlines one by one.

An Aug 15 roundup of how the biggest Wall Street banks use AI (Business Insider, via DNYUZ) laid the numbers out:
- JPMorgan: nearly 1,000 AI use cases running, an in-house generative AI platform rolled out to 200,000-plus employees, and $2B invested in AI, which the bank says it has matched in savings.
- Citi: a $12B tech budget, nearly 9 in 10 employees using AI tools, and 4,000 staff trained as internal "AI stewards".
- Morgan Stanley: its own DevGen.AI saved developers 280,000 hours of legacy-code grunt work.

Notice what almost none of that money buys: a prediction of tomorrow's close. It all goes to one job — handing "read it, sort it, cross-check it" to machines, so humans only make the final call.

The retail-vs-institution gap was never about access to information. Same filings, same headlines. The gap is processing cost: they have a department of AI reading for them; you have whatever time is left after work.

MarketDaily is built on that logic: Monday to Saturday, 7am for Taiwan stocks and 8pm for US stocks, one email with the market picture, 5 curated stories, sector rotation, and your own holdings (up to 80). Earnings dates flagged, major news the day it lands, and 30 AI chat messages a day to interrogate any of it. What's left for you is the last step — the judgement.

We also publish every call and settle it in public once its horizon is up, including the ones we got wrong, with confidence intervals on the numbers and the raw dataset open for you to recompute. Showing the misses is how you earn the right to be believed on the hits.

Everything is free for now at NT$0, no credit card needed. If charging ever returns, subscribers who join now keep free access permanently.

Do you check the market first, or your inbox first? Tell me below.

drafts.caption_zh:
我把同一個持股問題丟給 AI 兩次:第一次它稱讚我眼光很好,第二次它一口氣列出 3 個我不想聽的理由。差別只在我多貼了一段話。

AI 預設是順著你講的。你說「我手上這幾檔應該還行吧」,它就幫你找理由支持——這叫陪聊,不叫做功課。

想讓它變成有用的功課夥伴,直接複製這段貼在你的問題前面:

「請以最嚴格的空方研究員身分回答。不要安慰我,不要做平衡報導。針對我列出的公司,各給我 3 個最可能讓它營運或評價被下修的理由;每一個都要指出可查證的來源類型(財報欄位、產業出貨數據、法說會說法),並標註你自己信心最低的那一點。最後回答我一句:要出現什麼樣的證據,我才該承認自己看錯?」

為什麼有效,三個關鍵:
① 指定角色——不指定,它就選最討喜的那個。
② 禁止安慰——把「平衡報導」這條退路先堵掉。
③ 要「我看錯的證據長什麼樣」——這一步最重要,它把閒聊變成一個可以被推翻的假設,而不是心情按摩。

兩個提醒:AI 報的數字一律回原始財報自己對一次,它很會編;還有,這是幫你把問題想深,不是叫你買賣什麼。

我們固定在做的就是這件事的自動版:台股班早上 7:00、美股班晚上 20:00,週一到週六寄進信箱(週日休息),幫你把功課先做完——大盤摘要、板塊輪動、財報提醒,還有 AI 助手每日 30 則。全功能限時免費 NT$0,未來恢復收費後,現在訂閱的早鳥用戶永久保留免費使用權。

你是習慣自己開 AI 問一輪,還是讓功課早上 7:00 自己送到信箱?在下面告訴我。
drafts.caption_en:
I asked AI the exact same question about my holdings twice. The first time it told me I had great instincts. The second time it fired back 3 reasons I did not want to hear. The only difference was one paragraph I pasted in front.

AI defaults to agreeing with you. Say "my positions are still fine, right?" and it will go find reasons to support you. That is chatting, not homework.

To turn it into an actual research partner, copy this and paste it before your question:

"Answer as the strictest short-side research analyst you can be. Do not reassure me and do not give me a balanced take. For each company I list, give me 3 of the most plausible reasons its business or valuation could be revised down. For every reason, name the type of verifiable source (a line item in the financial statements, industry shipment data, something said on the earnings call), and flag the single point you are least confident about. Finish with one line: what evidence would have to show up for me to admit I was wrong?"

Why it works, three keys:
1. Assign a role. If you do not, it picks the most agreeable one.
2. Ban the reassurance. Close off the "balanced take" escape route up front.
3. Ask what being wrong would look like. This is the important one. It turns small talk into a hypothesis that can actually be knocked down, instead of a mood massage.

Two warnings: always check any number the AI gives you against the original filing yourself, it makes things up freely. And this is for thinking a question through, not a call to buy or sell anything.

What we do on a fixed schedule is the automated version of this: the Taiwan session at 7:00am, the US session at 8:00pm, Monday through Saturday (Sunday off), straight into your inbox with the homework already done for you. Market recap, sector rotation, earnings reminders, plus 30 AI assistant messages a day. Everything is free right now at NT$0, and when we do restore charging, everyone who subscribes now keeps free access permanently as an early subscriber.

Do you run your own AI round yourself, or would you rather the homework land in your inbox by 7:00? Tell me below.

drafts.caption_zh:
漏看新聞不可怕,把假消息當真的,才會真的賠到錢。

所以我們的日報前面擋著一道過濾層,只做四件事:

① 回推出處——一則消息找不到原始來源,就不進日報,不管它標題多好看。
② 交叉對照——同一件事跟其他來源兜不起來,標成「待查」,不會被寫成結論。
③ 互相挑錯——活下來的內容讓多個 AI 互相反駁,再由裁判取捨,撐不住反方的說法會被拿掉。
④ 事後認帳——判斷過的都留在網站戰績頁,連判錯的那幾筆一起公開,附信賴區間與校準表。

第四件事才是關鍵:過濾層會不會失手,不是靠嘴巴講,是攤開紀錄讓你自己查。

週一到週六早上 7 點寄到信箱,你的持股最多 80 檔一起顧。全功能限時免費開放;未來恢復收費後,現在訂閱的早鳥用戶永久保留免費使用權。

你比較怕漏看新聞,還是比較怕看到假的?在下面跟我說一句。
drafts.caption_en:
Missing a headline isn't the expensive part. Believing a fake one is.

So there's a filter layer sitting in front of our daily brief. It does four things:

1. Trace the source - if a claim can't be traced back to an original source, it doesn't make the brief, no matter how good the headline looks.
2. Cross-check - if the story doesn't line up with other sources, it gets flagged as unverified instead of written up as a conclusion.
3. Argue it out - what survives gets challenged by multiple AI models, with a judge deciding what stays. Anything that can't hold up against the counter-argument gets cut.
4. Own the record - every call stays on our public track-record page, including the ones we got wrong, with confidence intervals and a calibration table.

The fourth one is the whole point: whether the filter misses isn't something we get to just claim. The record is open for you to check.

In your inbox at 7am, Monday through Saturday, tracking up to 80 of your holdings. Everything is free for a limited time; when paid plans return, everyone who subscribes now keeps free access permanently as an early subscriber.

Which scares you more - missing the news, or reading a fake version of it? Tell me below.

drafts.caption_zh:
對手花幾千塊開戶獎金買你下載 App。我們連一個「升級才看得到」的按鈕都沒有。

券商廣告現在長一個樣:送你獎賞、送你免佣、強調小錢也能買美股。全都在比誰把錢丟得更快。沒有人敢談另一件事——你收到的內容,跟「有付錢的人」收到的到底一不一樣。

MarketDaily 的產品裡找不到那道鎖。不是我們大方,是法律不准:我們沒有投顧牌照,依法任何個別股票的解讀都不能因為誰付了錢就變多、變深、變早。所以我們乾脆把它做成產品鐵則——個股分析對全體用戶完全相同,不因付費而有任何差別,一個字都不會少給你。

同一套邏輯也用在戰績頁:判對的跟判錯的放在同一頁,錯的留著不刪,還附上信賴區間讓你自己去對。敢把自己看走眼的攤在陽光下,才有資格談信任。

現在全站零收費、不需要信用卡,全功能限時免費;未來恢復收費後,現在訂閱的早鳥用戶永久保留免費使用權。週一到週六早上 7 點台股班、晚上 8 點美股班,自己的持股最多 80 檔都幫你顧著。

你上一次被「升級才解鎖」擋在門外,是在哪個 App?在下面告訴我一個。
drafts.caption_en:
Rivals spend thousands in sign-up bonuses to buy your download. We do not even have an "unlock with upgrade" button.

Broker ads all look the same right now: cash rewards, zero commission, pitches about how little it takes to start buying US stocks. Everyone is racing to throw money at you. Nobody wants to touch the other question - is what you receive the same as what a paying user receives?

There is no lock inside MarketDaily. Not out of generosity, but because the law says so: we hold no investment advisory licence, so the read on any individual stock may not become more, deeper or earlier just because someone paid. We wrote it in as a product rule - single-stock analysis is identical for every user, never differentiated by payment, and nothing is held back from you.

Same logic on the track record page: the calls we got right and the ones we got wrong live on one page, misses kept rather than deleted, with confidence intervals so you can check us yourself. Showing where we were wrong is what earns the right to talk about trust.

Right now the entire site costs NT$0, no credit card needed, all features free for a limited time; when pricing returns, early-bird subscribers who join now keep free access permanently. Monday to Saturday, 7am for the Taiwan session and 8pm for the US session, covering up to 80 of your own holdings.

When was the last time an "upgrade to unlock" wall stopped you, and in which app? Tell me one below.

刷牙那 3 分鐘,台股美股就聽完了 🎧

同業搶著用開戶獎金買你下載一個 App。我們給的東西土多了——時間。

每個交易日早上 7:30、晚上 8:30,AI 把當天日報濃縮成一集 3 分鐘語音快報:大盤怎麼走、兩則必知新聞、板塊往哪邊轉,講完剛好。通勤、洗漱、開車等紅燈都能聽,眼睛不用離開路面,行情已經進腦袋。

訂閱的人還會多一集「你的專屬快報」:兩句帶過大盤,剩下的時間全給你自己盯的那幾檔(最多 80 檔)。

週末休息,週六早上改給文字版週末回顧,不硬湊集數。

價格 NT$0,全功能限時免費開放;未來恢復收費後,現在訂閱的早鳥用戶永久保留免費使用權。

🎧 marketdaily.ai/audio 公版快報打開就能聽,不用註冊。

你是讀派還是聽派?在下面告訴我一句,我想知道哪邊人多。
drafts.caption_en:
Brushed my teeth. Already done with the TW and US markets. 🎧

Other finance apps are paying you a cash bonus to download them. We offer something far less glamorous: your morning back.

Every trading day — 7:30 AM for Taiwan, 8:30 PM for the US — our AI condenses that day's full briefing into one 3-minute audio brief: where the index went, the two headlines that mattered, which sectors money rotated into. That's the whole thing.

Listen while commuting, getting ready, or waiting at a red light. Your eyes stay on the road; the market still gets in.

Subscribers also get a second episode, "your personal brief": two lines on the broad market, then the rest of the time goes to the tickers you actually track (up to 80 of them).

Weekends off. Saturday morning gets a written weekly recap instead; we don't pad the feed.

Price: NT$0 — every feature, free for a limited time. If paid plans ever return, everyone who subscribes now keeps free access permanently as an early subscriber.

🎧 marketdaily.ai/audio — the public edition plays right away, no signup.

Reader or listener? Tell me below which one you are; I want to know which side wins.
